stance.label: Short-term bearish · long-term valuation in the bottom zone

headline: Loss-taking has spread from short-term to long-term holders and 62K was tested; selling is deepening, and below it the next line is 60.5K.
summary: Short-term bearish: the three-day range broke down, active selling returned, ETFs lost another $240M on Nov 17 and 73% of accounts are still long. Long-term bullish: only 46% of supply is in profit and unrealized profit has sat below the cycle floor for 5 days, a valuation seen only in past cycle-bottom zones. Below a 62K close few coins sit down to 60.5K, where long-term holder losses would set a cycle high; it takes a run of ETF inflows to say buyers are back.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 7 straight closes below; a close back above needs +15.5%

overview.lead: The three-day range broke to the downside: the close at 62,985 is a new low for the leg from Sep 21, and the intraday low touched exactly 62,000.
points: Intraday range 62,000–64,928, closing in the lower third; volume was 1.3x the 20-day average.
Fear & Greed at 11, a sixth day of extreme fear; the FOMC minutes leaned hawkish and the S&P 500 fell for a fifth day.
Over two months BTC is down 22.1% against 8.3% for the Nasdaq: crypto fell first and fell further.
Neither the market stage nor the framework did anything new today (see the exit page).

cycle.lead: Valuation got cheaper and the trend did not turn: more than half of supply is at a loss and the Dawn Index stays in Deep Night.
points: This page's finding: supply in profit is 46.4%, under 50%, a level earlier cycles only reached in bear-market bottom zones (Bitview, Nov 18).

Market stage is bull, day 41, with 1 of 6 evidence lights on (exchange supply); the 200-day MA at 72,720 is only 0.2% above its level 30 days ago, and if it flattens further the premise of this stage gets tested.
Dawn Index heat 7.3, Deep Night; weekly bull-bear score −0.72. They measure different things: valuation is cheap, trend points down.
Tidemark bottom signal 38.1, still short of 50; the Jun 30 low at 58,525 is under test until Dec 19 and is 7.1% away.

market.lead: This leg made a new closing low: down 27.3% from Sep 21, deeper than most down legs of this cycle, with no reversal close yet.
points: The close fell to the 6.3rd percentile of the past year, below the 10% line at 63,542; the last three cycle lows all sat inside this kind of zone, but after first entering it price fell a further 35%–52% within a year.
Sell Pressure Index at 100 for a 9th day with momentum at 0.07, so the bottom combo is still on; 20 cases since 2012, price up 30 days later in 11, about the same as any day.
The leg-end line at 72,432 is 15.0% away.

deriv.lead: Options bought the protection back while long accounts did not leave: the inversion widened from 1.6 to 3.4 points and Binance long accounts are at 73.5%.
points: Yesterday we wrote the inversion was nearly gone; today it reversed: 7-day implied vol 45.8% vs 90-day 42.3%, and the 25Δ risk reversal at −6.54 makes downside protection dearer.
Leverage did not retreat with price: open interest is up 5.9% in 30 days while price fell 23.0% (Coinalyze); weighted funding is 3.85%.
Estimated dealer gamma is most negative at 60,000, about $19.5M of same-direction hedging per 1% move, so a slide toward it would amplify swings (Deribit, estimated).

The estimated long-liquidation band at 60.8–62.0K (2.6% below the close) is nearer than the short band at 65.4–67.1K above; the order book shows $233M of bids in the 62,000 bucket, on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The money that came back for a day left again: ETFs lost $242.8M on Nov 17 and active spot selling returned.
points: ETFs are −$2.86B over 20 sessions, the deepest of this stretch; the June stretch reached −$5.64B (CoinMarketCap).
Takers on three spot venues net sold 1,335 BTC on the day after net buying 2,510 BTC yesterday; Coinbase spot takers net sold 10,531 BTC over 7 days (Coinalyze).
Stablecoin supply is $286.3B, down $16.2B in 30 days; realized cap is −0.52% over 30 days, a fifth day below zero (DefiLlama, CoinMetrics Nov 17).
Korea premium is back at 2.27%; USDT at 0.9986 to the dollar, so stablecoins keep being cashed out to dollars.

onchain.lead: Short-term holders are no longer the only ones selling at a loss: LTH-SOPR fell from 0.86 to 0.73 in a day, and the 7-day aSOPR is the lowest since the series began in Nov 2023.
points: This page's finding: long-term holders realized $2.74B of losses over 7 days, up from $1.91B yesterday; their loss share is 43.9%, 1.5 points from this cycle's 45.4% peak (Bitview, CheckOnChain).
Short-term holders realized 11,701 BTC of losses against 1,885 BTC of profit; day 9 of capitulation, intensity 3.65.
About 390K BTC moved at a loss over these 7 days and the 64K bucket gained 270K BTC; that batch is under water today as well (Bitview).
Miners are not forced sellers yet: hashrate at 983 EH/s is still rising, but the breakeven for 20 J/TH rigs at $0.06 power is 62,426, 0.9% below the close.

exit.lead: Nothing new under the framework today: the hedge buy-back was already met yesterday, and the MVRV Z 7-day average slipped to 0.44 (CoinMetrics, Nov 17).
points: 7 straight closes below the 200-day MA at 72,720, 13.4% under the line.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.437, far from the 0.75 line (111,512); the three top indicators read 12 / 12 / 35, all low.

news.title: FOMC October minutes: almost all participants saw further hikes as likely appropriate, some wanted 25 bp at that meeting and a couple floated a larger move in December; the vote was 10-2 to hold at 3.75%–4%
news.read: The hike is priced; what is new is the size. Polymarket has a December hike at 97.7%, of which 6.2% is for 50 bp or more. The 2-year yield sits 0.8 points above the policy ceiling, a tight backdrop that lines up with stablecoins shrinking $16.2B in 30 days. No change to the cycle read.

news.title: S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 7,323.63, a fifth straight loss and a break of its 200-day average; Dow −1.1%, Nasdaq +0.4%, the dollar at a 19-month high and gold down 3.51%
news.read: On a strong-dollar day gold and BTC fell together: BTC lost 2.9%. Over two months BTC is down 22.1% against 8.3% for the Nasdaq, still the weakest of the group; if stocks catch down, the 62K layer gets tested again.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost about $240M on Nov 17, with IBIT at −$209.5M, a day after IBIT took in $76.5M
news.read: Our CoinMarketCap series shows −$242.8M, the same direction and size. Yesterday we wrote that outflows had stopped and inflows had not started; correction: outflows stopped for one day. The 20-session total is −$2.86B, the deepest of this stretch.

news.title: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range, selling 980M shares for about $80B; it lists on Nasdaq as ANT on Nov 19
news.read: The largest IPO on record lands in the same week as BTC's drop, and media reports carry the line that the IPO is draining crypto money; coincidence is not cause. What our data shows is the result: stablecoins down $16.2B in 30 days and ETFs −$2.86B over 20 sessions. Whether those two turn after the listing matters more than the first-day pop.

news.title: Citi cut its 12-month BTC target to $99,532 from $113,000, citing weaker ETF demand, lower market activity and a less supportive macro backdrop
news.read: We do not publish targets, but its reasons match our readings: ETFs are −$2.86B over 20 sessions and the estimated ETF holder cost sits 20.2% above the close. Sell-side targets follow price down and do not move the flow numbers.

news.title: Talos: the long-spot, short-perp basis trade yields only 3%–5% a year, near or below Treasury yields; five of the six most traded BTC options are puts, led by the Dec 4 $60,000
news.read: Our Deribit basis median is 5.34% against a 3-month bill at 4.15%, so the carry is barely a point and that money has no reason to return. The Dec 4 60,000 put holds 5,761 BTC of open interest, the largest strike of that expiry; open interest does not tell buyers from sellers.

news.title: CoinDesk: a weekly drop of 12%+ through the 200-week average has happened only 3 times since 2013 (Aug 2015, Mar 2020, Jun 2022); price was higher three months later each time, after first falling another 10%–17%
news.read: Only 3 cases, and the June 2022 one was followed by the FTX leg down. It fits our read: valuation is in the bottom zone, the timing of a bottom is not here yet. Of the 5 times more than half of supply was at a loss in our data, 2 were followed by a further drop of 30% or more.

news.title: CryptoQuant weekly: BTC is back in a bearish phase after losing the 200-day and 365-day averages; Bull Score 10, 62,000–65,000 as possible support, and 72,900 and 75,900 to reclaim for a recovery
news.read: Our rule-based market stage is still bull, day 41, because the 200-day MA is higher than 30 days ago; the definitions differ, the reading is the same: the close is 13.4% below the 200-day MA at 72,720. Its 62–65K support zone is our two thickest short-term holder buckets.

findings.title: Loss-taking spreads to long-term holders; 62K is the last thick layer
findings.lean_why: Loss-sellers now include long-term holders, so selling is still deepening, and few coins sit below 62K to absorb it.
findings.what: Who sells below 62K, and who buys? The sellers have already changed: long-term holders are selling at a loss too, with LTH-SOPR down from 0.86 to 0.73 in a day (Bitview, Nov 18).
findings.why: Start with who is selling. Short-term holders are still the bulk: 11,701 BTC of realized losses against 1,885 BTC of profit on the day, with 94.2% of their coins under water. Long-term holders are the new part: $2.74B of realized losses over 7 days, up from $1.91B yesterday; network-wide 7-day aSOPR is 0.964, the lowest since the series began in Nov 2023, and realized profit ÷ realized loss was 0.123 on the day (CheckOnChain). Loss-taking is also heavier than at the last low: the peak this time is 14.5 bp of market cap against 5.4 bp on Sep 15. Then the cost map: the two thickest short-term holder buckets are 62–64K with 670K BTC and 64–66K with 650K BTC, and today's close sits at the lower edge of the first; 60–62K holds only about 70K short-term holder BTC. Against 30 days ago: short-term holders grew from 3.65M to 3.83M BTC and long-term holders shrank from 16.45M to 16.28M BTC (Bitview, actual coin age); coins with a cost above 88K, a zone price never revisited, fell by 130K BTC, which can only be loss-selling. By estimate, the largest bucket of coins bought in these 30 days and not yet moved sits at 64K with 440K BTC (estimated; the model is 2.1% off the actual short-term holder total). Some buyers are visible: by address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 38K BTC in 7 days while the 1K–10K tier shed 36K BTC; the order book shows $233M of bids in the 62,000 bucket. Money says the opposite: ETFs lost $242.8M on Nov 17 and spot takers net sold 13,084 BTC over 7 days (Coinalyze).
findings.alt: Another reading: part of the long-term holder loss-selling is coins bought above 80K in May–June that just crossed 155 days, so by nature still this cycle's high buyers and not old coins giving way; LTH-SOPR is a single-day value and its 7-day average is 0.88. Bitview data is per-UTXO with no entity clustering, so exchange wallet housekeeping counts as loss-selling; address tiers are not entities.
findings.history: A lower price with bigger loss-taking has mostly come late in a decline, though often not for the last time. This combination has occurred 58 times since 2013, with price higher 30 days later in 44 and a median of +6.9% (any day: +2.8%). The 7-day aSOPR reaching the bottom 2% of the past year has happened only 3 times since Nov 2023, followed by −8.5%, −26.0% and +5.2% over 30 days. In all three past bear markets long-term holder losses were largest at the bottom; this cycle's largest so far is 0.292% of market cap on Jun 30, against 0.217% now.
findings.so: What changed is who is selling: the past two weeks were short-term holders washing out, and today long-term holder loss-selling grew too, while the freshly turned-over coins at 62–66K are themselves under water. What did not change is the price structure: thick above 62K, thin below. If the close reached 60K, 98.5% of short-term holder coins would be under water and long-term holder coins at a loss would rise by about 270K BTC; at an estimated 60,500 the long-term holder loss share would exceed this cycle's 45.4% peak. The market stage and the framework do not look at this finding.
findings.next: By Nov 23: a close below 62,000 means the thickest layer failed too, and the next meaningful levels are 60.5K and the Jun 30 low at 58,525. By Nov 25: the LTH-SOPR 7-day average back at 1 or above means long-term holder loss-selling stopped and this round was only short-term holder turnover.

findings.title: More than half of supply at a loss: bottom-zone valuation, but not yet the timing
findings.lean_why: More than half of supply at a loss with unrealized profit under the cycle floor has only appeared in cycle-bottom zones; twice, though, price fell 30%+ further after entering it.
findings.what: Is this price cheap? Yes, and cheap in the way only earlier bear-market bottoms were: just 46.4% of supply is in profit, down from 68.4% a month ago (Bitview, Nov 18).
findings.why: Three independent measures point the same way. Supply in profit is below 50%, with the close under the 63,930 cost line at which half of supply is in profit. Relative unrealized profit is 33.8%, a fifth day under the 35% floor, lower than the 34.5% of Jun 30 and a new low for 2026. Of all supply 53.6% is at a loss, and today price broke the first loss floor (about 63,600; only 5% of days in history had more supply at a loss). CoinMetrics agrees: MVRV 1.21 and NUPL 0.17, both near the 12th percentile of four years (Nov 17). The conflict is in trend and money: realized cap is −0.52% over 30 days and one-year cumulative net realized profit/loss is still falling, so loss-taking has not stopped.
findings.alt: On-chain valuation may be blunter in the ETF era: ETF shares change hands off-chain, unrealized profit at this cycle's top only reached 56% against 66%–83% in the prior three, and the floor may have shifted with it. Supply in profit is also sensitive to turnover at the top of the range: 390K BTC moved at a loss over 7 days, mostly into 62–65K, and a small further drop flips that whole batch to a loss, so the share falls faster than price.
findings.history: More than half of supply at a loss has always been a bear-bottom-zone condition, but the stay varied a lot: 243 days in the 2015 cycle, 85 in 2018, 45 in 2022 and 21 this June. The first loss floor has been broken only 5 times since 2012: April 2014 and November 2018 were followed by further drops of 52% and 34%, March 2020 was the low itself, November 2022 fell another 15% and this June another 4%. Relative unrealized profit under the floor has also occurred in only 5 stretches, the longest being 255 days in 2015.
findings.so: What changed is the long-term valuation read: from cheap to a level only bottom zones have had. What did not change is the short term: cheap valuation does not hold price up by itself, someone has to buy, and today's flow numbers do not show that buyer. This does not contradict the headline: valuation speaks to months and longer, the spread of loss-taking to these few weeks.
findings.next: By Nov 25: supply in profit back above 50% (a close above roughly 63,930) means this was a brief dip into the zone, like this June; a break of the second loss floor (about 60,930) means the path is the 2018 kind, breaking floor after floor.

research.summary: Glassnode published only a methodology piece on order-book rewrite speed on Nov 18, with no new Week On-chain since Nov 17; the 62K line from that Nov 17 issue was touched intraday today, and our readings are weaker than when it wrote.

items.title: Book Churn: How Fast the Order Book Is Being Rewritten
items.points: A new metric, Book Churn: how often order-book price levels are revised per ten minutes, scored against the same hour over the prior 30 days. A score of 2+ is followed by an above-median-volatility hour 63.2% of the time (50% baseline), statistically level with a price-range signal at 63.7%; it has no direction and peaks with the move, not before it.
items.meaning: A methodology piece with no BTC price levels. The reminder for us is that order-book walls get rewritten fast: today's $233M of bids in the 62,000 bucket is a snapshot, not support that is bound to hold.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: BTC fell to 62K on Nov 15 and realized losses reached levels not seen since early 2023; 62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder coins; the remaining long-liquidation cluster is 59.5–62.2K; ETFs lost $2.6B over ten trading days; reclaiming 74.1K would look like a bottom forming, a daily close below 62K points to 58.5K and the Realized Price at 53.7K.
items.meaning: Its lower line at 62K was touched intraday today and held on the close. Our Realized Price is 53,559, close to its 53.7K; its point that selling was absorbed needs a discount today, since active selling came back.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week and briefly broke 63K; futures open interest $34.2B, the lowest since August; 25Δ skew 13.7%, the highest since August; ETFs lost $995M on the week; short-term holder NUPL −7.4%; its conclusion is that leverage was flushed and the market is less crowded.
items.meaning: We disagree on less crowded: Binance long accounts are at 73.5% and open interest is up 5.9% in 30 days while price fell 23%. Our short-term holder NUPL is −18.2% (Bitview, Nov 18), deeper than when it wrote.

items.title: Bitcoin Back Where the Rally Began
items.points: BTC is down six straight weeks, back in July's 61,300–67,000 base; 60–65K holds about 1.4M BTC and 55–60K only about 305K; base case this week 61,800–69,400 with a lean to retesting 62,029; three straight ETF inflow days, STH-SOPR back at 1 and a reclaim of 72,700 would mark a recovery.
items.meaning: The retest of 62,029 happened today with a low of 62,000. None of its three recovery conditions is met: ETFs lost money again on Nov 17 and STH-SOPR is 0.974.
